newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin heart operation said ended successfully.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin heart operation said ended successfully.

text.p: Russian officials said President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation on Tuesday had been completed successfully and the 65-year-old president was fine.
A source in the Cardiology Research Centre, where the operation was carried out, said surgery had gone well.
"Everything was fine, great," he said. Asked about Yeltsin's condition after the bypass surgery, he replied: "He is OK".

RIA and Interfax news agencies quoted sources in the government and in the Kremlin as saying the operation had been completed successfully. Interfax quoted a Kremlin spokesman as saying it had lasted seven hours.
Kremlin officials had said after six hours of surgery that there had been no complications and surgery was going according to plan.

The bypass operation will improve the supply of blood to the Russian president's heart and allow him to lead a normal life. But doctors say the days immediately after surgery are crucial to deciding whether Yeltsin will make a full recovery.
Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year and doctors say he may have had a third one before the second round of the presidential election on July 3.
The president said in a statement issued before the surgery began that he was confident that it would go well.
The operation was carried out by top Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin, assisted by a dozen specialists. Western doctors, including U.S. bypass pioneer Michael DeBakey, were monitoring the proceedings.
